question: Can next-word prediction on text teach a model how the world works?
differ: One side says next-word prediction at scale forces models to capture the world's structure; the other says text prediction or imitation is too thin to build real understanding.

sides.label: Next-word prediction forces world understanding
sides.stance: Predicting the next word well requires understanding the universe, and simple objectives at massive scale yield emergent complexity.

sides.label: Text and imitation alone aren't enough
sides.stance: Learning from text and imitation alone doesn't give real understanding of the world.

question: Does reinforcement learning give models new strategies or only boost existing skills?
differ: One side says RL lets thinking models discover new strategies like backtracking; the other says RL only makes the model more consistent at answers it already sometimes gets right.

sides.label: RL discovers new thinking strategies
sides.stance: Reinforcement learning lets thinking models discover strategies such as backtracking that are hard to hardcode by hand.

sides.label: RL only boosts existing abilities
sides.stance: Quoting a DeepSeek paper, RL only makes a model answer correctly more consistently, and cannot teach rules the model lacks, such as how pieces move.
